title: Requiem for a Dream
events_chronological: Harry Goldfarb pawns his mother Sara's television for drug money, and Sara buys it back from the same shop every time.
Harry, his friend Tyrone and his girlfriend Marion plan to buy weight, cut it, and use the profit to open a shop for Marion's designs.
Alone in her Brighton Beach flat, Sara is telephoned with news that she has been chosen to appear on a television game show.
Sara cannot fit into the red dress she wore to Harry's graduation, and starts a diet of grapefruit and hard-boiled eggs.
Harry and Tyrone make their first good buy, and the money starts coming in.
A doctor prescribes Sara amphetamines without examining her, and the weight starts falling off.
Marion breaks with her parents' money and starts drawing again, and she and Harry imagine the shop together.
Tyrone is caught up in a shooting at a street deal, and the supply dries up across the city.
Sara doubles her pills, starts grinding her teeth, and hallucinates the refrigerator advancing across the kitchen.
Harry's arm becomes infected at the injection site, and the three of them start using more than they can sell.
Marion sleeps with her psychiatrist Arnold for money to buy drugs.
Tyrone is arrested in a raid, and Harry spends the last of their money bailing him out.
Starving and alone, Sara hallucinates herself onto the game show and is jeered at by the studio audience.
Sara walks to the television company's offices in a stained coat and collapses in reception.
Harry and Tyrone drive to Florida on a rumour of pure heroin, with Harry's arm turning black on the way.
Marion goes to the dealer Big Tim and takes part in a sex party for a bag of heroin.
Sara is committed, force-fed and given electroconvulsive therapy while her friends wait outside the ward.
Harry's arm is amputated at a Florida hospital, where the police are called about the needle marks.
Tyrone is put on a Southern prison work gang, sick with withdrawal and dreaming of his mother.
Each of the four curls into the same foetal position - Harry in his bed, Marion clutching her bag, Sara staring at a screen, Tyrone in his bunk.
syuzhet_notes: The film is divided into three captioned seasons and moves forward through them, cutting between Sara's flat and her son's world often enough that the two declines run in step. Its nonlinearity is less reordering than compression and intrusion: montages of a few seconds stand in for weeks, and Sara's hallucinations at told-order bullets 8 and 13 are staged as though they were happening. The last movement cross-cuts all four collapses into one continuous sequence.
fabula_notes: Time passes in jumps marked only by the season captions, so the intervals between events are inferred rather than stated. The game show, the refrigerator and much of what Harry sees are hallucination rather than event, and are placed here at the point in each character's decline at which they occur.
